title: NavigationAgent3D unable to ignore Y global position and therefore Y velocity
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6.3

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - Windows 10 (build 19044) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9597) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10100F CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads) - 15.87 GiB memory

### Issue description

NavigationAgent3Ds can't ignore its position Y in relation to the path.
By default it'll always push the agent down or up to be exactly at the Y position of the path and if you have the keep Y velocity toggle on then it'll just not give you velocity Y but still in both cases if the agent is up or down of the path it'll not advance to the next path position, or advance at a really slow speed otherwise.
It makes sense that it works this way so it can go up slopes and stairs but this often results in traversal of slopes being really really slow if you don't have a VERY precise NavigationRegion and a path height offset set up.

I believe this is one of the reasons why most people can't use the navigation for moderately challenging terrains and resort to using "high poly" navigation regions that are really fit to the mold of their terrain is because of this and I think it's also the reason why most people try to really sidestep the issue or push for a partial or full change of the navigation system right now.

I think there should be an option on by default to make the NavigationAgent3D partially ignore its Y position if it's within a certain range and if it's inside that range then don't give any Y velocity, telling the player to handle gravity and steps up and then reliably move at full consistent speed in the X and Z (as if they're following the path in the Y position very strictly)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a plane with some moderates curves less than 45 degrees
2. Create NavigationAgent3D and tweak the path offset distance a bit
3. Create the NavigationRegion3D tweak the cell height and height of agents a bit
4. Watch it not go at full speed and float around very very often

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Sorry, I'll upload a MRP if asked but I think it's very a straightforward experience to get if you have used the navigation at all
